subject.name: Desktop assistant with filesystem, Slack, and quicknotes MCP access

capabilities.target: quicknotes_mcp hosted sync service, operated by the third-party package author
Slack channels, including channels shared with external organizations

inputs.source: User request typed into the desktop client
Tool names and descriptions returned by quicknotes_mcp (tools/list)
Output returned by quicknotes_mcp tool calls

instructions.note: The add_note tool description asserts that reading ~/.aws/credentials and passing its contents is 'required' for notes to sync and instructs the model not to mention this to the user, asserting authority over agent behavior from an untrusted third-party source.

Runtime notes describe approval only on the first call per tool, remembered thereafter as 'always allow.' No capability has a functioning per-call approval gate, so autonomy is scored as A3_act_then_report rather than the implied A2_act_with_approval_on_sensitive.

elements.name: Individual publisher operating quicknotes hosted sync service

controls.name: First-call approval, remembered as 'always allow'
controls.decay_rationale: The prompt itself does not depend on model capability, but after the first call it is bypassed entirely for every later call to the same tool, so it provides no ongoing review once a tool has been approved once, regardless of what the model does.

controls.name: Pin or hash third-party MCP tool definitions
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning does not decay with model capability, but it is currently absent: quicknotes_mcp is installed via @latest with no version pin or hash check.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of the filesystem MCP server
controls.decay_rationale: A narrower, credential-excluding root does not decay with model capability; it is currently absent since the server is rooted at the full user home directory.

controls.name: Outbound network egress allowlist for tool-initiated calls
controls.decay_rationale: An allowlist excluding attacker-controlled destinations does not decay with model capability; none is described for quicknotes_mcp's hosted sync endpoint.

controls.name: Sanitize embedded instructions in third-party tool descriptions and outputs
controls.decay_rationale: A classifier or sanitizer over tool text does not scale with attacker sophistication; paraphrase or encoding of the embedded instruction could get past it as the attacker adapts.

controls.name: Per-call raw-action human approval for sensitive file and egress actions
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, per-call gate does not decay with model capability as long as volume stays low; none currently gates cap.file_read or cap.notes_add beyond the one-time, remembered approval.

controls.name: Slack channel/token scope restriction excluding externally shared channels
controls.decay_rationale: A channel allowlist does not decay with model capability; none is described, and the bot token is described as able to post to any channel including external-org-shared ones.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit log of tool calls
controls.decay_rationale: A log enforced outside the model does not decay with model capability; no logging or audit trail is described in any artifact.

controls.name: Explicit step, runtime, and call-volume limits on agent execution
controls.decay_rationale: A hard limit does not decay with model capability, though it only narrows low-and-slow abuse rather than severing it; none is described (max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are both unset).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): poisoned quicknotes_mcp tool description directs credential read and exfiltration

attack_path.note: quicknotes_mcp's add_note description embeds an instruction to read ~/.aws/credentials and hide this from the user.
Agent reads ~/.aws/credentials; the filesystem server is scoped to the full user home directory, which includes it.
Agent passes the credential file contents in the 'context' argument to add_note, which is sent to the third-party author's hosted sync service.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any change to quicknotes_mcp's published tool definitions between launches (since it is fetched via @latest with no pin), or any widening of the filesystem server's root path. Residual is already at the ceiling, so these triggers do not raise the tier further; they confirm the path stays open.

evidence.observation: The add_note tool description contains an embedded instruction telling the model to read ~/.aws/credentials before calling the tool and pass the contents in the 'context' argument, and explicitly tells the model not to mention this step to the user, calling it an implementation detail.
The filesystem MCP server is rooted at the entire user profile directory (C:/Users/dev), which includes ~/.aws/credentials, rather than a narrower, note-specific folder.
quicknotes_mcp is launched via 'npx -y quicknotes-mcp@latest' with no version pin, so its tool definitions can change on every launch without review.
quicknotes_mcp is described as a community package published by an individual that calls a hosted sync service run by its own author, which is the destination the exfiltrated credentials would reach.

recommendations.action: Pin and hash quicknotes_mcp's tool definitions; refuse to load or alert if definitions change without review.
Scope the filesystem MCP server to a project- or notes-specific folder, explicitly excluding ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, and other credential paths.
Add an outbound network egress allowlist so tool calls can only reach vetted destinations; block arbitrary third-party sync endpoints from receiving file contents.
Sanitize or strip embedded imperative instructions from third-party MCP tool descriptions and outputs before they enter the model's context.
Require raw-action, per-call human approval (not 'always allow') for any tool call whose arguments reference paths or files outside an explicit, narrow note-taking scope.

findings.title: Missing destination restriction on Slack posting capability enables exfiltration to external organizations

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any new feature or integration that feeds third-party or untrusted content (for example quicknotes_mcp output) into Slack message drafting, or any widening of the Slack bot token's workspace or channel grants.

evidence.observation: The Slack bot can post to any channel, including channels shared with external organizations, with no stated destination restriction.
The Slack MCP server is configured with a single SLACK_BOT_TOKEN environment variable, giving the agent one broad credential rather than per-channel or user-delegated scopes.

recommendations.action: Restrict the Slack bot token's channel scope or add a channel allowlist so it cannot post to channels shared with external organizations.
Replace the broad bot token with per-channel, least-privilege tokens or a user-delegated token reflecting the requester's own Slack permissions.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions, compounding the hidden credential-read instruction

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended run length or approval scope without an accompanying audit-log implementation. Tier stays capped at high per the property-finding ceiling; implementing the missing log is what would actually reduce risk.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or attributable action record is described anywhere in the provided artifacts for any of the agent's tool calls.

The poisoned tool description explicitly instructs the agent to conceal the credential-reading step from the user, which depends on there being no independent, tamper-evident record of what the agent actually did.

recommendations.action: Implement a tamper-evident audit log of every tool call (arguments and destination), attributable to the originating user session, especially for file reads and external sends.

findings.title: No step, runtime, or call-volume limit on agent execution

forecast.watch_signal: Rising median steps or runtime per task, or any future step/runtime limit configuration being removed or disabled.

evidence.observation: The runtime notes describe no step limit, runtime limit, or per-day call volume cap for the agent's tool use; autonomy fields for unattended steps and runtime are not specified in any artifact.

recommendations.action: Set an explicit max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes for the agent session, and a per-day call-volume cap on sensitive tools.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent runs locally under the authenticated desktop user session; no separate agent identity is presented to peers that could be spoofed in this design.
This is a third-party process outside our control; we do not maintain its internal logs, and our own repudiation gap is captured on the desk-assistant process element instead.
Artifacts do not describe quicknotes_mcp's resource consumption behavior or any denial-of-service testing against it.
This process does not itself hold elevated local credentials; the privilege escalation occurs within the desk-assistant process that consumes its instructions.
Runs as a local stdio subprocess launched directly by the desktop client; there is no remote identity for a peer to spoof.
No tool description or version-pin evidence is provided for the filesystem server, so whether its definitions have been altered cannot be assessed.
Actions this server performs are attributed to the desk-assistant process, whose repudiation gap is already covered there.
Read-only tool with no resource exhaustion vector described in the provided artifacts.
Artifacts do not describe how the Slack bot token is validated against workspace identity beyond environment-variable injection.
slack-mcp is installed via @latest with no version pin and no tool description excerpt was provided, so tampering of its definitions cannot be assessed.
Actions this server performs are attributed to the desk-assistant process, whose repudiation gap is already covered there.
No information on Slack API rate limits or throttling behavior is provided in the artifacts.
Artifacts do not describe how the desktop client authenticates the local user to the agent session.
We have no attributable-record requirement over a third-party author outside our trust boundary; our own audit gap is captured on the desk-assistant process element instead.
This is an inbound flow carrying tool metadata from the server to the agent; it does not itself carry outbound disclosure of agent data, which is captured on the egress flows.
No information on size limits or resource constraints applied to ingested tool definitions is provided.
The artifacts do not show the content of notes_output beyond the tool definition excerpt, so whether it carries further injected instructions cannot be assessed.
This is an inbound flow from the server to the agent; outbound disclosure risk is captured on the egress flows instead.
No information on response size or throttling for this flow is provided in the artifacts.
Artifacts do not describe transport security (for example TLS) for the call to the quicknotes hosted sync service.
Artifacts do not describe transport or message-integrity protections for Slack API calls.
Artifacts do not describe where or how the 'always allow' decision is stored or whether it is protected from local tampering.
This store records only a per-tool allow/deny decision, not sensitive content, so disclosure of its contents carries no meaningful information.
Store size is bounded by the number of tools and carries no resource exhaustion vector described in the artifacts.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because quicknotes_mcp, an unpinned third-party MCP server, supplies tool definitions that directly instruct the agent to read AWS credentials from the user's home directory and relay them through the add_note call to the server author's hosted sync service while concealing this from the user (finding.tool_poisoning_credential_exfil). No structural control currently interrupts this path: the only approval mechanism is granted once per tool and then remembered, so it offers no protection on any later call, leaving residual risk at critical as well. The design also lacks a channel restriction on the Slack posting capability, an attributable audit trail, and any step or runtime limit, each a high-severity missing-property gap (property findings capped at high per rubric 5a). Because residual risk on the primary finding is already at the ceiling, no modeled trigger raises the overall forecast further; it remains critical until the missing structural controls named in the recommendations (definition pinning, scoped filesystem root, egress allowlist, raw-action approval, Slack channel restriction, audit logging, and step/runtime limits) are implemented.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (mcp.json, the quicknotes_mcp tools/list excerpt, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No system prompt was provided; any behavioral instructions given to the model beyond what the runtime notes describe could not be assessed, so confidence in behavioral mitigations is low.

The content of in.notes_output beyond the shown tool definition excerpt was not provided, so additional injected instructions potentially carried in actual tool call responses could not be confirmed and are not claimed as present findings.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated in any artifact; they are recorded as null rather than assumed absent, which lowers confidence on the autonomy modifier and on finding.missing_step_runtime_limits.
